a tactical card game about shared washing machines

Laundromat

3–6 players · ages 12+ · 45–135 minutes
Shoes first, then dark, then light. the one line that runs the whole game
Dark Shoes
Dark Socks
Light Shirt
Light Hat
Dark Pants
Ten items each Not enough washers First one done wins

Pages 2 to 7 teach the game in pictures and take about five minutes. Pages 8 to 12 are the reckoning — the heart of it. From page 13 it is a card reference to flip to mid-game. The last page tears out as a player aid.

Provisional — the name
“Laundromat” is a working title and is used throughout this booklet. It is a genericised former trademark, almost certainly unregistrable, and there is already a published game with the name. A rename before art or layout money is spent is expected — it is a find-and-replace here. Every unsettled rule in this booklet is fenced in an amber box like this one, or carries an amber provisional tag. They are gathered on the last page.

What you are doing

You have ten pieces of laundry. So does everyone else.
There are not enough washers.

Once a day, every washer decides for itself

Some of what is inside washes. The rest goes back to its owner's hand, with no penalty. Nothing is ever lost.

Damp
You will see these three stamps all game.
WASHED — into your clean pile, for good.
BACK — to your hand, unharmed.
DAMP — socks only. They stay in the washer.
4

First player with all ten clean wins, immediately

Checked after the whole day's washing has finished. If two people finish on the same day, they both win.

Nothing is hidden except the cards in your hand. This is a puzzle you solve out loud, not a bluffing game. A dark sock thrown in at the last moment can ruin a whole machine for everybody — and everybody can see it coming.

The dot tells you the shade

Solid = dark Open ring = light

Silhouette, not just tone, so it survives bad light and colour-blindness. The dot's colour is who owns the card.

Shade is not owner colour. Every player's colour has dark cards and light cards. “Dark” is about how dirty the wash gets. Your colour is about who the card belongs to.

Two words worth learning now

Clothes — shoes, socks, pants, shirt, hat.

Linen — underwear and blanket.

A card of socks is a pair, and counts as one item. Most rules just say item, meaning any of the fourteen.

Settled — damp needs no component
There is nothing to mark. Socks in a washer with a blanket do not wash and stay in that washer, so damp is something you read off the board rather than a state that travels with a card. No token, no zone, no player mat.

Nothing in the design says. No default has been picked. Standard options: whoever did laundry most recently · the youngest player · at random. One line of text is needed before print.

Setup4
the spine of the game
A day

The game is played in days. Every day runs the same five steps.

1

Roll phase — everyone takes one turn

The keyholder goes first, then round to the left. Yesterday's keyholder goes last. The order rotates with the key.

each player's turn, in order — you may not go back
1–6
Roll the die

It tells you how many items you must load, and what else happens.

Play one card (optional)

At most one ready card, and only before you load. Never a card you drew today.

Load — mandatory

Put exactly as many items into washers as you rolled. Fewer only if you truly cannot.

Resolve the die's extra

The move on a 4, the card draw on a 5, the event on a 6.

Cards before laundry. The card comes first because the Mesh bag has to be open before anything goes in it. Everything else about the order follows from that.
2

Event — if one was drawn today provisional

Only the first 6 rolled each day draws an event card, and it is turned face up the instant it is drawn. At most one event per day.

3

Key — the keyholder switches one washer

One on, or one off, or nothing. Not both. Not two. The single most valuable action of the day.

4

Reckoning — every washer that is ON runs

This is where laundry gets washed. Washers that are off, destroyed, or occupied by Jimothy do not run at all. See the next five pages.

5

End of day

Fresh cards become ready. The key passes to the left. If anybody has ten clean items, they have already won.

Settled — when a drawn event happens
The moment it is drawn, in the middle of the drawer's turn. Players yet to go play into the changed board; a Coin or a Snacc played later the same day can answer it. Where a washer must be named — the Gang, Jimothy — the player who drew the card names it.

step one of your turn
The die

One six-sided die. It decides how much laundry you must put in — and hands out the game's three surprises.

1
Load 1 item
2
Load 2 items
3
Load 3 items
The most laundry you can move in one day.
4
Load 1, then move any one item between washers
Anybody's item, including your own. The destination must legally accept it. Not out of Jimothy's washer, and never into or out of a destroyed one. The move is optional; the load is not — and because the move comes after you load, it cannot free a slot for your own item.
⇄
5
Load 1, then draw two special items and keep one
The other goes to the bottom of the deck. Your card sits face up in front of you — everyone sees it, and you cannot play it today.
Mesh bag
6
Load 1, then draw an event
Only the first 6 rolled each day draws one. Any later 6 just loads an item. The card is turned face up the instant it is drawn — everyone sees what is coming.
Jimothy
A custom die is recommended, printing the action straight onto the face: LOAD 1 / 2 / 3, LOAD 1 + MOVE, LOAD 1 + CARD, LOAD 1 + EVENT. It removes the only lookup a new player makes every single turn.
The die6
step three of your turn · not optional
Loading

Put exactly as many of your items into washers as you rolled. They may go into the same washer or different ones. Loading is not optional.

A washer will take your item — unless one of these five

✕
It is full.
Four items is the limit, at every player count.
✕
It has been destroyed by the Gang.
Gone for good. Neither a source nor a destination for anything.
✕
Jimothy is in it.
A raccoon. Nothing goes in, nothing comes out.
✕
There is a blanket inside and your item is not socks.
✕
Your item is a blanket and the washer holds anything other than socks.

That is the whole list.

Blankets need a washer to themselves — except for socks

Legal ✓
Blanket
Socks may share with a blanket, in both directions.
Refused ✕
Blanket
A shirt cannot go in beside a blanket. Nothing but socks ever can.
Socks do not wash in a washer holding a blanket. They stay in it. Not clean, not back to you — they sit in the drum as ordinary dirty socks and wash on the first night that washer runs without a blanket. The rule keys on the blanket being in there, not on the blanket itself washing. See page 12.
A washer that is switched OFF can still be loaded. It just will not run, and it carries everything inside into tomorrow.

When you cannot load

You load fewer than you rolled only when:

  • your hand holds fewer items than that, or
  • no washer on the board will accept anything you hold.

Then you load as many as you legally can, which may be none. No penalty, no re-roll, no substitute action. Say so out loud so the table can see it, and move on. This is a real situation, not a technicality — after a Circuit break nothing drains and everyone keeps loading.

the heart of the game · read it once now, once after your first day
The reckoning
Shoes first, then dark, then light. everything below is that line, spelled out

Every washer that is ON runs

Each one decides, item by item, what comes out clean and what comes back. Washers that are off, destroyed, or occupied by Jimothy do not run at all.

Nothing is ever lost

What washes goes to its owner's clean pile, permanently. Everything else goes straight back to its owner's hand, with no penalty of any kind. After a washer has run, it is empty.

One washer at a time

Washers never affect each other, so resolve them in any order. Order inside a washer never matters either.

Find the highest rung that another player's item occupies in that washer. Your item must be on that rung or higher. If it is lower, it goes back. That is the whole cross-player rule — your own other items are simply not consulted.

Your shirt comes back. Blue's dark pants sit on rung 3. Your light shirt is on rung 4, which is lower.

Both of yours wash. Their hat comes back. The highest rung an opponent occupies is 4. Your dark pants clear it, your light shirt matches it — and your own two items do not fight each other. Meanwhile Pink sees your dark pants on rung 3, above them.
The two ladders in one line. The room ranks by shoes and shade. Your own pile ranks only by category. An item washes only if it survives both.

Shoes beat everything, including other dark items. A's dark shoes, B's light shirt, C's dark pants → only A's shoes wash. C's dark pants are on rung 3 and lose to rung 1, even though they are dark.

Your own items never protect you. A's dark shirt, A's light shirt, B's dark shirt → A's light shirt sits on rung 4 under B's rung 3, so the room sends it back. Your own pile is judged separately, and never shields you from the room.

stage three of three
The filters

An item that has cleared both ladders can still be sent back by one of these four. Check them last.

Underwear

Underwear washes only in a washer holding nothing but underwear. Anything else in there — anyone's, yours included — and your underwear comes back.

Underwear
Washed
Underwear
Washed
Underwear
Back
Washed

Both A's. On the right the shirt outranks the underwear on A's own ladder and breaks isolation. It is your own laundry that ruined it — nobody did this to you.

Blankets

A blanket must be alone, except that socks may share with it. The loading rules make this almost impossible to break. If a washer somehow holds an illegal blanket mix, nothing in it washes.

Blanket
Washed
Damp

Both Tan's, both in Tan's top category, nobody else in there — so both would have washed. But socks that wash beside a blanket are never clean the first time. See page 12.

Crowding provisional — may be cut

If other players have put two or more items of the same type as yours into that washer — three of a type in total, counting yours — then yours is crowded out and comes back. Any colour, any shade; only the type matters. Your own copies never crowd you.

Three shoes cancel out. A's dark shoes, B's dark shoes, C's dark shoes and D's light shirt, exactly full → nothing washes at all. All three pairs clear the room, then crowding sends all three back; D's shirt is not rescued, because crowding sends items back and never promotes anything.

Coloring

If another player has played a Coloring card on the washer, your items there are ruined and come back — unless you have a Color catcher on that washer.

A's light shirt, B's light pants, C's light hat, with a Coloring played by A and a Color catcher played by B → A and B wash, C goes back. Everything is light, so the ladder would have washed all three. The catcher protects its owner and nobody else.

Provisional — does crowding survive at all?
Current default: crowding is in, as printed above. It fires in roughly one reckoning in a hundred and it has not been decided whether it earns its rules text. If it is cut, delete the crowding panel above, line 5 of the checklist below, the crowding line on the back page, and the two worked examples that use it. Nothing on any card changes.
The reckoning · the filters10
the reckoning, all together
The full check, in order

For each item in a washer that is running, its owner asks — all clear → it washes. Any one fails → it goes back.

1
The room. Is it on the highest rung any other player's item occupies here, or higher?
dark shoes → light shoes → dark → light
2
Your pile. Is it in your top category here?
shoes → clothing and blankets → underwear · shade ignored
3
Underwear. If it is underwear, is everything else in the washer also underwear?
4
Blanket. If a blanket is here, is it alone but for socks?
5
Crowding. Do other players have two or more of the same type here? provisional
6
Coloring. Is there an opponent's Coloring here that you cannot catch?
7
The Mesh bag — overriding every line above.
Anything in a Mesh bag washes, full stop. provisional
Each owner is judged separately, so one washer can resolve at several levels at once. Work through it owner by owner rather than trying to settle the whole drum in one glance.

What the cards do to it

Three special item cards attach to a washer and are read when it runs.

Bleach

Swaps every shade in the washer before the room's ladder is read. It does not disarm shoes — bleached dark shoes are light shoes, and light shoes still beat everything that is not a shoe. No effect on your own category ladder, which never looked at shade.

Sanitizer

Switches off the two shoe rungs. Shoes become ordinary items ranked on shade alone, for everyone in the washer — and among your own items, shoes drop down to sit with clothing.

Coloring & catcher

As on the previous page: Coloring ruins every other player's laundry in the washer; a Color catcher saves its own owner from it and nobody else.

Sanitizer, and what it costs. A's dark shoes, B's light shirt, C's dark pants, Sanitizer by B → A's shoes and C's pants wash; B's shirt goes back. B played it and still lost their own shirt.

Bleach does not stop shoes. A's dark shoes and B's light shirt with a Bleach → the shoes still wash, the shirt still goes back. Bleach changes shade, never category.

The full check11
the rest of the reckoning
Damp socks, dead machines, the key

Damp socks

Socks do not wash in a washer that holds a blanket. They stay in the washer.

They do not come back to you and they do not go to your clean pile — they sit in the drum as ordinary dirty socks, taking up one of that washer's four places. The first night that washer runs without a blanket in it, they wash normally. If somebody loads a blanket in again first, they stay again.

The rule keys on the washer containing a blanket, not on the blanket washing. If a blanket is in there, socks do not wash — end of story. Socks the wash sends back are different: if the ladder rejects them they come back to your hand like any other rejected item. Only socks that would have washed stay behind.

Machines that do not run

StateRuns?Can be loaded?How it got thereHow it gets out
ONyesyesthe defaultkey, Coin, Circuit break
OFFno — keeps everything insideyeskey, Coin, Circuit breakkey, Coin
Jimothyno — contents held hostagenothe Jimothy eventSnacc, Animal control

An OFF washer carries its contents into tomorrow untouched. Everything loaded into it just piles up.

Winning

The moment a player's clean pile holds all ten of the items they were dealt, the game ends and they win. Victory is checked after the whole reckoning has finished, never in the middle of it. If two or more players complete their tenth item on the same day, they all win together. There is no tie-break.

The key

The keyholder goes first in the roll phase, and takes the key step each day, after the events and before the reckoning: switch one washer on, or one washer off, or pass. Not both. Not two. At the end of the day the key passes to the left.

Switching a washer off protects what is inside — nothing washes, but nothing comes back either, and it carries into tomorrow. Switching one on is how you recover from a Circuit break. Switching off a washer Jimothy is in does nothing at all. It is the single most valuable action of the day. Do not waste it.

Damp socks · dead machines · the key12
card reference · flip here mid-game
Special item cards

Twenty cards, seven kinds, one shared deck. You get them by rolling a 5.

Drawing

Draw two, keep one, put the other on the bottom of the deck. The card you keep sits face up in front of you — it is fresh, and cannot be played today. At the end of the day it becomes ready and joins your hand.

Playing

On your turn, before you load, you may play one ready card. Coin and Snacc happen at once. The other five attach to a washer, do their job once when it runs, then go back into the deck and are shuffled in. A card at a washer that never runs is wasted.

Coloring

Coloring

Play on a washer. When it runs, every other player's laundry inside is ruined and goes back.

Your own laundry is not ruined — but nothing else protects it either.

Coloring attaches to a washer and waits there until it runs. Every item belonging to a player other than you is then sent back, whatever the ladder said. Your own items are untouched by Coloring, but they still have to survive the ladder and the filters like everyone else's — Coloring is not armour. If two players both play Coloring on the same washer, each ruins the other, and only a player holding a Color catcher gets anything out of it.

Color catcher

Color catcher

Play on a washer. Your laundry inside is safe from Coloring.

Protects you only, and only from Coloring.

Color catcher cancels Coloring for your items in that washer — including a Coloring played after yours, and two Colorings at once. It protects nobody else, and it does nothing against the ladder, crowding, underwear, blankets or shoes. If no Coloring is ever played there, the card is wasted.

Bleach

Bleach

Play on a washer. Until it runs, every item inside counts as the opposite shade: dark counts as light, light counts as dark.

Shoes are still shoes. Bleach swaps shades, nothing else.

Bleach flips the shade of everything in the washer — including your own laundry — before the ladder is read. It does not disarm shoes: dark shoes become light shoes, which are still shoes and still beat every non-shoe item in the washer. Two Bleaches on the same washer do not cancel out; the swap happens once.

Provisional — the wording, not the rule
The brief's older shorthand — “light items wash, dark items are sent back” — gives the wrong answer whenever shoes are present. The wording above is the swap the rule actually is, and the brief has been corrected. Nothing to decide but whether you like the sentence.
Special item cards13
card reference
Special item cards, continued
Mesh bag

Mesh bag provisional

Play on a washer as you load. Everything you put into that washer this turn goes in the bag, and all of it washes when the washer runs — whatever else is inside.

Only what you load this turn, only into this washer. Not what was already in there.

Play the Mesh bag before you load, then load as normal. Every item you put into that one washer on that turn is bagged. When the washer runs, bagged items wash — the ladder, crowding, underwear isolation, blanket exclusivity and Coloring all lose to the bag. Items already sitting in the washer from an earlier day are not bagged, nor is anything you load elsewhere, nor is anything anyone else loads. Bagged items are still in the washer for everyone else's purposes: your bagged dark shoes wash for certain and still wreck the wash for the other players.

Provisional — three open questions on one card
The brief flags the Mesh bag as comfortably the strongest card in the game, with no counterplay; a predecessor card was cut in an earlier draft for exactly this.
  • (a) Keep, weaken, or revert? The v8 fallback text is written and intact: “Play on a washer as you load. Underwear you load into it this turn washes here even among other garments. Underwear already inside is not protected.”
  • (b) Do bagged items still set the ladder and count for crowding for everyone else? Currently yes.
The printed name is Mesh bag; both codebases still call it Wash net internally.
Sanitizer

Sanitizer

Play on a washer. Shoes count as ordinary clothes in this wash.

Helps whoever it happens to help — including your opponents.

Sanitizer attaches to a washer and switches off the two shoe rungs of the ladder. Shoes are still washed or sent back, but only on shade, exactly like a shirt or a pair of pants. It also flattens shoes on your own ladder: with a Sanitizer up, your own shoes no longer outrank your own shirt. Every other rule is untouched. It affects the whole washer, not just you, so it can hand two opponents a wash. A Sanitizer on a washer holding no shoes does nothing.

Special item cards14
card reference
Special item cards, continued
Coin

Coin

Turn any one washer on or off, right now. You do not need the key.

One use, then back to the deck. The keyholder still acts later today and can undo it.

Played on your turn like any other special item, and resolves at once: pick any washer that is not destroyed and flip its power. It is spent immediately and shuffled back into the deck — it is not kept, and it is not a second key. Because the keyholder acts after every player has taken their turn, the keyholder can switch your washer straight back.

Snacc

Snacc

Move Jimothy to any other washer. Everything he was sitting on goes back to its owners, unwashed.

Only playable while Jimothy is on the board.

Snacc lures the raccoon out of the washer he is in and into any other washer that has not been destroyed. The items he was holding hostage are released — released, not washed: they go straight back to their owners' hands. His new washer immediately becomes unusable and anything already sitting in it becomes hostage. You cannot play Snacc when Jimothy is not in play.

Provisional — how many of each
The deck is exactly 20 cards — a real manufacturing constraint, since 84 item + 4 event cards are fixed and 108 is the sheet-efficient total. The split across the seven kinds is unset. The app ships a flat 3/3/3/3/3/3/2 that its own config labels arbitrary and explicitly not a recommendation; the simulation still runs 14 cards, two of each. No count appears on any card. Circuit break is now settled, so this is blocked behind the Mesh bag decision alone.
Three points that catch people out. The Mesh bag covers only what you load this turn, into that one washer — yesterday's items are not in the bag. Bagged items are still in the washer for everyone else. And the Coin is not a second key: it is spent the moment it is played, and the keyholder acts last.
Special item cards15
card reference
Event cards

Four cards, one of each. The first 6 rolled each day draws one; later 6s do not. At most one event happens per day, and the card is turned face up the instant it is drawn.

Gangart pending
Gang

Gang

Choose a washer. The gang hides behind it and shoots it. It is out of the game for good, and everything inside goes back to its owners.

Leave this card on the wreck. Gang happens once per game and never returns to the deck.

The player who drew the card chooses the washer. Its contents return to their owners' hands unwashed, and the washer is destroyed: it can never be loaded, run, or switched on again, and the board is one washer smaller for the rest of the game. If the chosen washer is the one Jimothy is sitting in, the hostages are released as normal and Jimothy relocates to another surviving washer — the same player chooses where.

Circuit breakart pending
Circuit break

Circuit break

The power trips. Nothing washes tonight. Every washer keeps what is inside it, and everything is back to normal tomorrow.

Circuit break cancels tonight's reckoning and does nothing else. No washer changes power, so there is nothing to switch back on and no recovery to manage — the next night runs exactly as it would have. Every washer keeps its contents, loading carries on as normal, Jimothy is untouched, and a destroyed washer stays destroyed. It costs everybody one night.

Settled — this was one of three
The deleted faces were V2 “all off” (every washer off, keyholder restores one per day — the face this booklet used to print) and V3 “auto-restore” (all off, all back at the end of tomorrow). The old recommendation was V3 and should not be re-cited: its smoke test had an invalid control and measured the event timing that has also been replaced.
Event cards16
card reference
Event cards, continued
Jimothy

Jimothy

A raccoon moves in. Choose a washer: it cannot run and cannot be loaded, and everything inside is stuck with him.

Only Snacc or Animal control move him. Leave this card on the washer.

The drawer chooses which surviving washer Jimothy settles in. That washer is out of service: it does not run at the reckoning, nothing may be loaded into it, and items already inside cannot be taken out by a roll of 4. Those items are hostages, released — unwashed — only when Jimothy leaves. Neither Gang nor Circuit break removes him; Gang destroying his washer makes him move, it does not get rid of him.

Animal controlart pending
Animal control

Animal control

Jimothy is taken away. Everything stuck with him goes back to its owners, unwashed.

If Jimothy is not on the board, nothing happens.

Animal control removes the raccoon from the board at once and frees his washer for use from the next load onwards. The hostages are returned to their owners' hands, not washed — players expect this card to save their laundry and it does not. If Jimothy is not in play the card does nothing at all, which is roughly half the time.

Which cards come back. Circuit break, Animal control and Jimothy's card go back into the event deck after they have done their work — though Jimothy's card stays out on the washer while he is in play. Gang does not come back, ever.

Odds and ends

Two washers cannot affect each other. Resolve them in any order you like.

Order inside a washer never matters. There is no “first in, first out”. Every item is judged against the same contents.

A card played at a washer that never runs is wasted — off, empty or destroyed, it makes no difference. The card still returns to the deck.

Switching off a washer Jimothy is in does nothing. It already could not run, and you have spent the key on it.

Animal control does not save your laundry. Hostages come back unwashed. Every player expects otherwise once.

A Coin can be overruled. It resolves during your turn; the keyholder acts later the same day.

Everything on the floor is public. Machine contents, clean piles, fresh cards, markers, Jimothy, the wreck. Only your hand and ready cards are yours.

Nothing is ever destroyed except washers. No item card ever leaves the game once it is dealt.

Event cards · odds and ends17
every one of these is a real board that came up
Tricky reckonings

“A's dark shoes” means the item belongs to player A.

The washer holdsWhat happens
1 · Shoes beat everything, including other dark items.
A's dark shoes · B's light shirt · C's dark pants		 A's dark shoes wash. Everything else goes back. Dark shoes are the top rung. C's dark pants are on rung 3 and lose to it, even though they are dark.
2 · Your own two shirts are friends. An opponent's shirt is not.
A's dark shirt · A's light shirt · B's dark shirt		 Only A's dark shirt washes. A's light shirt is on rung 4 with B's dark shirt on rung 3 above it, so the room sends it back — your own items never protect you from someone else's. B's dark shirt clears the room, but there are now three shirts and two of them are A's, so crowding takes it. crowding provisional
3 · Underwear is the hardest thing in the game to wash.
A's dark underwear · A's dark shirt		 The shirt washes. The underwear goes back. Twice over: clothing outranks underwear on A's own ladder, and underwear only ever washes in a washer holding nothing but underwear. It is your own laundry that ruined it.
4 · Underwear alone is fine, and shade still bites across players.
A's dark underwear · A's light underwear
then: A's dark underwear · B's light underwear		 Both wash — same category, shade is irrelevant among your own items.
Only A's washes. B is another player, so the room's ladder applies and dark outranks light.
5 · Three shoes cancel each other out. provisional
A's dark shoes · B's dark shoes · C's dark shoes · D's light shirt (full)		 Nothing washes at all. All three pairs clear the room's ladder, and then crowding sends all three back. D's light shirt is not rescued: crowding sends items back, it never promotes anything.
6 · A blanket, three pairs of socks, and nobody happy. provisional
A's dark blanket · A's dark socks · B's light socks · C's dark socks (legal, and exactly full)		 Only the blanket washes. Each pair of socks sees the other two beside it, which is three socks, so crowding takes all three. The blanket has only two socks beside it, which is not a crowd, and nothing outranks it. Since no socks washed, nobody even gets a damp partial.
7 · Damp socks, and the reading that surprises people.
A's light blanket · A's dark socks		 The blanket washes and the socks stay in the washer. Both are A's, both in A's top category, nobody else in the washer — but socks never wash beside a blanket. The blanket leaves clean; the socks are still in the drum tomorrow, and wash on the first night nobody puts another blanket in with them. This holds even when the blanket does not wash: the rule is about the blanket being in there.
Tricky reckonings18
real boards, continued
Tricky reckonings, with cards on the washer
The washer holdsWhat happens
8 · Sanitizer, and what it costs.
A's dark shoes · B's light shirt · C's dark pants · Sanitizer played by B		 A's dark shoes and C's dark pants both wash. B's light shirt goes back. With the shoe rungs switched off, the washer is decided on shade alone. Compare 1: the same washer, one card, two washes instead of one — and B played the card and still lost their own shirt.
9 · Bleach does not stop shoes.
A's dark shoes · B's light shirt · Bleach		 A's dark shoes still wash and B's shirt still goes back. The shoes read as light shoes and the shirt reads as dark — but shoes still outrank everything that is not a shoe. Bleach changes shade, never category.
10 · Coloring, and the one player who ducks it.
A's light shirt · B's light pants · C's light hat · Coloring by A · Color catcher by B		 A and B wash. C goes back. Everything is light, so the ladder would have washed all three; Coloring ruins everyone but A, and B's catcher saves B. The catcher protects its owner and nobody else.
11 · The Mesh bag beats the ladder but does not hide from it.
A's dark shoes in a Mesh bag · B's light shirt		 A's shoes wash — they were always going to — and B's shirt still goes back. The bag guarantees its own contents and changes nothing for anyone else. The shoes are still dark shoes as far as the room is concerned.
12 · The Mesh bag does not reach backwards.
A's underwear, sitting in a switched-off washer since yesterday · B's light shirt · A plays a Mesh bag today, loads nothing, and the washer is switched back on		 Both go back. The bag covers what you load on the turn you play it. Yesterday's underwear was already in there and is not in the bag, so underwear isolation takes it as usual.

the words this booklet uses
Glossary

Clean pile — where washed items go. Permanent. Ten ends the game.

Clothes — shoes, socks, pants, shirt, hat.

Crowding — three or more items of one type in one washer sending them all back. provisional — may be cut

Damp — what socks are while they sit in a washer that also holds a blanket: they will not wash tonight, and they stay where they are. Not a marker and not a lasting property.

Day — one full round: everyone rolls, the event happens, the key acts, the washers run.

Fresh — a special item card drawn today. Face up, unplayable until tomorrow.

Hostage — an item stuck in Jimothy's washer. Cannot wash, cannot move, released unwashed.

Item — any of the fourteen garment cards of one colour.

The key — the token that makes you go first and lets you switch one washer per day.

Linen — underwear and blanket.

Loading — putting an item from your hand into a washer. Mandatory.

Ready — a special item card from a previous day. Playable.

The reckoning — step 4 of the day, when every washer that is on decides what washes.

The room — the other players' items in a washer, and the ladder they impose on yours.

Rung — a step of the room's ladder: dark shoes, light shoes, dark, light.

Sent back — returned to the owner's hand unwashed. No penalty.

Shade — dark or light. Not the same thing as your colour.

Washer — one of the machines. Holds four items. Also called a machine.

Sorting your hand

Hands, washer contents and clean piles are laid out in this order, on the table and in the app. It changes no outcome — it is a teaching aid, and it lets a new player fan a hand correctly without being taught. A small corner numeral on each card is recommended.

1
Dark shoes
→
2
Light shoes
→
3
Dark clothing
and dark blanket
→
4
Light clothing
and light blanket
→
5 Dark underwear
→
6 Light underwear
Shade must be readable across the table, in bad light, by a colour-blind player, and on the back-lit edge of a fanned hand. It cannot ride on tone alone: print the word DARK or LIGHT on the face, and repeat a shape mark that differs in silhouette — a solid disc versus an open ring — in the same corner on every card. Owner colour is a separate axis and must never be confusable with shade.
Glossary · sorting your hand20
one day, start to finish
A full turn, played out

Four players: Red, Blue, Green, Yellow. Five washers. It is day 3, and Green holds the key.

Green goes first, because Green has the key. Green rolls a 2. Green has a Sanitizer ready since yesterday but nothing worth using it on, so no card. Green loads a dark shirt and a dark hat into washer 1, which is empty. Nothing else happens on a 2.

Yellow is next. Rolls a 5. Yellow plays a Mesh bag on washer 1 — before loading, which is the only time it works — then loads one item, a light underwear, into washer 1. That underwear is now in the bag. Then the 5: two cards off the top, a Snacc and a Bleach. Jimothy is not on the board, so Snacc would be dead weight; Yellow keeps the Bleach, which goes face up and cannot be played until tomorrow.

Red is next. Rolls a 6 — the first 6 today, so Red draws an event. It is Jimothy, turned face up at once. Red loads one item first, a light pants into washer 4. Then the event: Red chooses washer 3, which is holding two of Blue's items. Washer 3 will not run tonight and Blue's two items are hostages. (That timing is arm E1. Under E2 or E3, Jimothy would not settle until every player had finished their turn.)

Blue goes last, having held the key yesterday. Rolls a 4. Blue loads a dark sock into washer 1, then takes the move: Blue would love to pull the hostages out of washer 3, but hostages cannot be moved. Instead Blue lifts Green's dark hat out of washer 1 and drops it into washer 5, purely so that washer 1 has less dark in it.

Key step. Green looks at washer 2 — empty, on, useless — and at washer 1, which now holds Green's dark shirt, Yellow's bagged light underwear, and Blue's dark sock. Green leaves everything alone and passes.

Reckoning. Washer 3 does not run; Jimothy is in it. Washer 1 holds Green's dark shirt, Blue's dark socks, and Yellow's light underwear in a Mesh bag. Yellow's underwear: bagged — it washes, nothing else needs checking. Green's dark shirt: the highest rung any other player occupies is 3 (Blue's dark socks; Yellow's underwear is light, rung 4). The shirt is dark, rung 3, so it clears the room. It is Green's only item, so it is Green's top category. It washes. Blue's dark socks: rung 3 against rung 3. Clears. They wash — no blanket in there, so they come out clean rather than staying in the drum. Washer 4 holds Red's light pants alone: it washes.

End of day. Yellow's Bleach becomes ready. Nobody has ten clean items. The key passes from Green to Yellow, who will roll first tomorrow.

All three wash. Underwear beside a shirt and a pair of socks would normally be hopeless — the bag is why it is not.

for the designer, not the player
Rules that are not final

Everything marked with an amber provisional tag or fenced in an amber box, gathered in one place. Nothing on this list may go to print as it stands. Ordered by how much of the booklet each one changes. Three questions were closed in v10 — when a drawn event resolves, what Circuit break does, and whether damp socks need a component — and are gone from this list.

1
The game's name — decide first.
A placeholder throughout: genericised former trademark, almost certainly unregistrable, and a published game already carries it. Suggestion on file: Jimothy's Laundromat. Changes the cover, every folio, three places in prose, and every asset outside this booklet. Rename before any art or layout money is spent.
2
How many of each special item card is in the 20-card deck.
The total is a manufacturing constraint; the split is unset. No count appears on any card. Blocked behind the Mesh bag decision.
3
The Mesh bag — keep, weaken, or revert; and its remaining sub-question.
Comfortably the strongest card in the game, with no counterplay. Fallback “Wash net” text is intact on page 14. Sub-question: do bagged items still set the ladder and count for crowding for everyone else (yes)? Whether a bag saves socks from a blanket is no longer a question — the bag guarantees a verdict, and a blanket strands socks after the verdict. Changes page 10 line 7, page 14, and reckonings 11–12 on page 19.
4
Whether the crowding rule survives at all.
Fires in roughly one reckoning in a hundred, rarer still now that your own copies no longer crowd you. If cut, delete the crowding panel on page 10, line 5 of page 11, reckonings 5–6 on page 18, the back-page line, and the glossary entry. No card changes.
5
How the first keyholder is chosen.
Nothing in the design says, and nothing has been invented here. Page 4 step 5 carries the flag. One line of text is needed.
6
Bleach's card wording — decided in substance, not signed off.
The shade-swap wording on page 13 is the rule as implemented; the brief's older shorthand gave the wrong answer whenever shoes were present, and has been corrected. Nothing to decide except whether you like the sentence.
One more, from outside this booklet
“Own items don't taint own items” — the rule this booklet's whole stage-one ladder is built on — is live and fully tested in the app but is not in the brief. Two consequences to sign off: a washer no longer resolves at a single tier, since each owner can be on a different rung at once (page 11's checklist is the mitigation, and it needs testing on a real table with real strangers); and underwear isolation and crowding are now partly redundant. The booklet cannot be finalised while its central mechanic is absent from the ground-truth document.

And one production note. Underwear, blanket, Gang, Circuit break and Animal control have no art. They appear here as hatched “art pending” plates, matching what the app renders, rather than as holes.

Quick reference
Laundromat one per player

The day

  1. Roll phase — keyholder first, then left.
  2. Event — if one was drawn today. provisional
  3. Key — keyholder turns one washer on, one off, or passes.
  4. Reckoning — every washer that is ON runs.
  5. End of day — fresh cards ready; key passes left.

Your turn

1. Roll.  2. Play one ready card (optional).  3. Load — mandatory.  4. The die's extra effect.
